lesson: Modifications to 'settings.json' must be strictly formatted valid JSON and saved to disk to be recognized.
Core environment changes (e.g., Display Language, Theme) often require a window reload or restart to apply.
VS Code architecture supports one workspace per window. Opening multiple .code-workspace files requires separate window instances.

Many VS Code features require extensions: custom backgrounds need extensions, array/data visualization needs extensions, automated file creation on startup needs extensions. Check if functionality requires extensions before attempting through settings.
VS Code display language changes require language pack extensions to be installed. Built-in settings can only switch between already-installed language packs.
VS Code has no built-in data structure visualization in the editor. Visualizing variables (like numpy arrays) requires debugger mode with appropriate extensions or external tools.
